newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 7.0/8.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 7.0/8.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 7.0/8.0 percent on Monday morning after falling to six percent.
Dealers said an early central bank supply of 992 billion rupiah caused excess supply early in the month, keeping swap rates soft and driving short-term rates below par.
One-week money fell to 9.5 percent and one-month money to 12.75 percent. Dealers said overnight money would have softened further if the central bank had not offered overnight papers.
The central bank offered overnight bilateral papers (SBIs) at five percent, one-week at 6.5, two-week at 8.5 percent, one-month at 10.25 percent and three-month at 11.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 11.5 percent. Bond dealers said the market seemed to show signs of life after slowing significantly before the general election.
"People are starting to ask for lines again. I think we may see improved activity when things settle down," one said.
